newsitem.title: ITALY: North African immigrants held on Italian island.
newsitem.headline: North African immigrants held on Italian island.

text.p: Police said on Saturday they had detained nearly 150 immigrants trying to enter Italy illegally, a day after 99 North Africans were expelled for coming ashore on the island of Lampedusa.
Police said 143 immigrants were caught early on Saturday on Lampedusa, a tiny island south of Sicily, after making the short crossing from Tunisia.

The immigrants were from Tunisia, Morocco, Algeria and Lebanon, police said, and were due to be ferried to Porto Empedocle in southern Sicily, from where police said they would be sent back to Tunisia.
Police said 27 of the immigrants jumped overboard a half nautical mile off Lampedusa in an attempt to swim to shore but were hauled in by coast guard ships.
Nearly 1,500 foreigners seeking to enter Italy illegally have been detained on Lampedusa since January 1, police said.

On Friday, 99 Tunisians and Moroccans were forced to take refuge on the tiny island after their two boats almost sank in stormy seas. They were to be sent back to Tunisia, from where their boats came.

Separately, 14 Pakistanis and three Bangladeshis trying to reach Italy illegally were held by the coast guard in the northeast town of Chioggia after they crossed the Adriatic on a boat from Greece. The 17 were expelled from the country.
